reference: The independent man-db whatis CLI reads private legacy text indexes using an empty private -C configuration. The installed legacy backend matches prefixes even with -w; Bash-os retains its documented exact-name lookup, checked separately as a contract. Help, implementation version identity and no-name diagnostic text are custom contracts. Successful lookups and no-result/invalid-option statuses retain independent parity cases.
coverage: single exact-name lookup from a whatis index
Hyphenated names and explicit whole-name matching against a longer name
multiple query arguments and mixed hit/miss status behavior
Documented help and version identity; usage error statuses
Bash builtin type and short-description metadata contracts
exclusions: No generated man-db binary index or mandb database lifecycle is exercised; fixtures use the documented legacy MANPATH/whatis text index.
No deferred operation case is applicable: this loadable performs read-only lookup against a private relative fixture and requires no privileged or hardware-backed operation.

Bash-os retains exact-name matching. The installed man-db legacy text backend matches a name prefix both by default and with -w; this observed difference remains outside the parity claim. The exact boundary case is an explicit custom contract, not a passing GNU comparison.

cases.purpose: A straightforward exact name returns its complete whatis record.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - fixture alpha utility' > whatis
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf alpha; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis alpha; fi

cases.purpose: A conventional hyphenated manual-page name is looked up as a complete name.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
printf '%s\n' 'alpha-beta (1) - hyphenated fixture' > whatis
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf alpha-beta; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis alpha-beta; fi

cases.purpose: Verify the documented Bash-os exact-name contract: tool must not match toolbox. The independent legacy man-db backend matches both even with -w, so this is an explicit compatibility limit rather than a parity assertion.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'tool (1) - exact fixture' 'toolbox (1) - longer fixture' > whatis
MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis tool

cases.purpose: Several requested names each produce their matching record in one invocation.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - first fixture' 'beta (1) - second fixture' > whatis
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf beta alpha; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis beta alpha; fi

cases.purpose: A successful lookup alongside an absent name reports the hit and a miss diagnostic.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
printf '%s\n' 'present (1) - present fixture' > whatis
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf absent present; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis absent present; fi

cases.purpose: An index with no matching name returns GNU man-db status 16 and its diagnostic.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
printf '%s\n' 'known (1) - known fixture' > whatis
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf absent; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis absent; fi

cases.purpose: A missing whatis index is reported as a GNU no-result status 16.
cases.script:
: > manpath.conf
if [[ $(type -t whatis) == file ]]; then MANPATH=. whatis -C manpath.conf absent; else MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1 whatis absent; fi

cases.purpose: Verify the documented Bash-os help synopsis. Output from a different implementation is not a byte-equality oracle.
Verify the documented Bash-os implementation identity. Output from a different implementation is not a byte-equality oracle.
The loadable is registered as a Bash builtin, as required for this loadable interface.
Bash help metadata exposes the independent one-line description declared by the builtin contract.
cases.stdout: whatis - Display one-line manpage descriptions for NAME(s).

cases.purpose: Require usage failure status 1 and a diagnostic. The independent man-db implementation writes its no-name prompt to stdout; diagnostic wording and output channel are explicit interface differences.
Reject invalid usage before accessing any manual index; compare the man-db failure status.
